messages:
alex: Quick sync 17:00 PST deploy tomorrow. Draft release notes at https://docs.redwood/release/v2.14.1-draft 17:00 PT publish. Canary at 12:00 UTC, quiet window 11:45-13:30 UTC. Please flag anything that must be communicated to customers.

maria: Heads-up: there's a subtle behavior change in model-serving batching when using `--adaptive-batch` that can increase tail latency for very short (<8 token) requests. We should mention it under 'Behavior changes' and recommend using the SDK helper `client.batch_optimize(false)` as a compatibility workaround.

alex: good call. Add compatibility note, not a breaking step.

carter: Ops note: Dedicated customers on pinned fleets will keep `runtime@2026-01-27` until we schedule a controlled unpin. Add a note about expected timeline: "unpin rollout ~2 weeks after GA, contact SE for exceptions".

meera: I'm going to request a legal blurb review because the privacy page has a new KMS integration mention. Legal expects 24h review. Do we want to delay public announce until they sign off?

ops-oncall: timeline constraints: we can hold public announce up to 18:00 PST if needed without breaking other schedules. Oncall coverage from 11:30-14:30 UTC. Pager duty group PD_Rollout on standby.

deploybot: /deploy canary v2.14.1-rc1 --targets=canary-16 --timeout=25m
deploybot: Canary started: v2.14.1-rc1 -> canary-16 (16 hosts). Observing health: 5xx, p99, cache-miss-rate.

maria: Canary metrics @5m: p99 +12%, p95 +4%, 5xx 0.02%. Looks like transient tail bump. Screenshot linked.

carter: If p99 goes above +40% for 10m or 5xx >=0.2% sustained 5m we promote rollback. Those are our thresholds for canaries with model-serving changes.

alex: add those thresholds to the release notes under "Rollback & criteria". Also include the manual approval flow: release owner + ops-oncall + eng lead.

meera: legal said the KMS blurb is fine if we add a short sentence about "customer-managed keys are optional and disabled by default." I'll paste the approved copy into the notes.

alex: pasted. Also adding a small "runbook" link: https://confluence.company/ops/runbooks/rc-rollout.

deploybot: Canary health update: 18m in 1 p99 settled to +6%, 5xx steady at 0.03%. No auto-rollback.

carter: Can we include a short note to support about expected customer questions: "why was runtime pinned?" and provide suggested one-liner: "pinned to reduce variability during rollout; we will unpin after stability window."

maria: Also add a 'rollback dry-run' step for the oncall checklist: practice the rollback command in staging and confirm permissions. I can run that at 09:00 UTC tomorrow.

ops-oncall: please do. I will be reachable and will escalate to SRE if needed.

alex: final internal announce copy (will post to #eng-releases at 16:45 PST):
"Internal heads-up: releasing v2.14.1-rc1 -> v2.14.1. Canary started and healthy; promoting to staged rollout at ~12:30 UTC pending stability. Quiet window 11:45-13:30 UTC. Key notes: runtime pinned on Dedicated; adaptive batching behavior change (compatibility workaround provided); KMS integration wording approved by legal. Rollback criteria and runbook: https://confluence.company/ops/runbooks/rc-rollout. Oncall: PD_Rollout. Public announce planned 17:00 PST. Questions in this thread"

carter: LGTM.

meera: LGTM from legal.

maria: LGTM.

alex: posting internal announce now and will wait for any last-minute edits. Thanks all.

deploybot: /announce internal "v2.14.1 staged rollout 12:00 UTC canary running, internal announce posted" --channel=#eng-releases --when=6834568860

alex: bot queued. Closing thread; continue monitoring in the pinned message.
